extracted.intended_audience: users of GAP (computational group theorists and mathematicians) working with character tables and representations
extracted.subtask_description: Reference specifications and behavioral requirements for GAP functions and methods dealing with character tables, decomposition matrices, printing/display, indicators, and algorithms (Dixon‑Schneider, representation computations).

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeXStringDecompositionMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeXStringDecompositionMatrix(modtbl[, blocknr][, options]) returns a string containing LaTeX code to print a decomposition matrix nicely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional options record may include phi, chi (strings for column/row label letters; defaults "{\\tt Y}" and "{\\tt X}"), collabels and rowlabels (subscripts; defaults are positions of Brauer and ordinary characters), nrows and ncols (max rows/cols per array; if present, each nrows×ncols portion is enclosed in \[ , \]), and decmat (if bound, must be the decomposition matrix to use rather than computing it from modtbl). AtlasLabelsOfIrreducibles may be used for Atlas tables to produce Atlas-compatible labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index (for two character tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Index(tbl, subtbl) returns the quotient of the Size values of tbl and subtbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Containment of underlying groups is not checked; distinction between Index and IndexNC (group index variants) is not made for character tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInternallyConsistent (for character tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsInternallyConsistent(tbl) checks consistency among stored attribute values of an ordinary or Brauer character table and returns true if no inconsistency occurs, false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ordinary tables checks: Size, SizesCentralizers, SizesConjugacyClasses; SizesCentralizers vs OrdersClassRepresentatives; ComputedPowerMaps vs OrdersClassRepresentatives; SizesCentralizers vs Irr; Irr (first orthogonality relation). For Brauer tables checks: Size, SizesCentralizers, SizesConjugacyClasses; SizesCentralizers vs OrdersClassRepresentatives; ComputedPowerMaps vs OrdersClassRepresentatives; Irr (closure under complex conjugation and Frobenius map). If inconsistencies occur they are printed when InfoWarning level >=1; final return value is false.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPSolvableCharacterTable
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPSolvableCharacterTable(tbl, p) determines whether the group underlying an ordinary character table tbl is p‑solvable; p must be a prime integer or 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default method uses attribute ComputedIsPSolvableCharacterTables to cache values and calls IsPSolvableCharacterTableOp to compute unknown entries. Synonyms IsPSolubleCharacterTable and Op variants exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsClassFusionOfNormalSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsClassFusionOfNormalSubgroup(subtbl, fus, tbl) returns true if the class fusion described by list fus corresponds to a subgroup U that is normal in G (tbl's group), false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: fus is a list of positive integers describing the class fusion of U into G. Example shows using PossibleClassFusions and testing each with IsClassFusionOfNormalSubgroup; typical use is to check normality from class fusion data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator (Frobenius‑Schur indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator(tbl[, characters], n) returns the list of n‑th Frobenius‑Schur indicators of the characters in list characters (default Irr(tbl)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ordinary tables ν_n(χ) = (∑_{g∈G} χ(g^n))/|G|. For Brauer tables in characteristic ≠2 and n=2, returns the second indicator. Computed indicators are cached in attribute ComputedIndicators; IndicatorOp computes unknown values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator behaviour in nonzero characteristic p and p=2
rubrics_metrics.description: Computation of Frobenius‑Schur indicators in nonzero characteristic uses special rules; in characteristic 2 some indicators may be unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For odd p, use Thompson‑Willems theorem. For p=2 necessary conditions used: trivial character has indicator 1; indicator is 0 iff character is not real‑valued; real characters outside the principal block have indicator 1; by [GW95,Lemma 1.2] any real constituent with odd multiplicity in the 2‑modular restriction of an ordinary irreducible with indicator 1 has indicator 1 if trivial character is not a constituent. If these conditions are insufficient an Unknown value is returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: NrPolyhedralSubgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: NrPolyhedralSubgroups(tbl, c1, c2, c3) returns the number and isomorphism type of polyhedral subgroups generated by elements from classes c1 and c2 whose product lies in class c3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classes c1,c2,c3 must be ordered according to the order of elements in these classes. If elements in class c1 and c2 do not generate a polyhedral group, fail is returned. Counts for V4, D2n, A4, S4, A5 can be derived from class multiplication coefficients and class Galois conjugates.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassMultiplicationCoefficient
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassMultiplicationCoefficient(tbl, i, j, k) returns the class multiplication coefficient c_{i,j,k} for classes i,j,k of the group with ordinary character table tbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: c_{i,j,k} equals the number of pairs (x,y) with x∈C_i, y∈C_j, and xy a fixed element of class k. In the center of group algebra KiKj = ∑_k c_{i,j,k} K_k. Given the character table, c_{i,j,k} can be computed by c_{i,j,k} = |C_i||C_j|/|G| · ∑_{χ∈Irr(G)} χ(g_i)χ(g_j)χ(g_k^{-1})/χ(1). Knowledge of class multiplication coefficients can be used to compute irreducible characters (see IrrDixonSchneider).

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassStructureCharTable
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassStructureCharTable(tbl, classes) returns the class structure n(C1,...,Cn) — number of n‑tuples (g1,...,gn) with g_i∈C_i and product 1 — for the classes listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length of classes must be at least 2. Computed by formula n(C1,...,Cn) = |C1|...|Cn|/|G| · ∑_{χ∈Irr(G)} χ(g1)...χ(gn)/χ(1)^{n−2}.

rubrics_metrics.name: MatClassMultCoeffsCharTable
rubrics_metrics.description: MatClassMultCoeffsCharTable(tbl, i) returns the matrix [a_{i,j,k}]_{j,k} of structure constants (class multiplication coefficients) for class position i of ordinary character table tbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for inspecting all coefficients with a fixed first index; example output given for L3(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: ViewObj (for a character table)
rubrics_metrics.description: ViewObj(tbl) prints a short identifier for the character table: "CharacterTable" followed by the identifier or, if known, the group in brackets; for Brauer tables the first string is "BrauerTable" and the characteristic is also shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the default ViewObj method for character tables and is used as lightweight display/identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrintObj (for a character table)
rubrics_metrics.description: PrintObj(tbl) behaves like ViewObj but uses the group's PrintObj instead of ViewObj for the group part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default PrintObj method for character tables mirrors ViewObj but delegates group printing to PrintObj.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display (for a character table) — default behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Display(tbl[, arec]) prepares character table data for columnwise output showing certain characters (by default all irreducible characters), orders of centralizers (factorized) and available power maps; printed characters are named X.n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of columns printed depends on line length (SizeScreen). First lines show orders of centralizers in factorized form; next line gives class names (ClassNames used if none stored). Power maps preceded by Pn show n‑th power maps in terms of class names. Ambiguous/unknown values displayed as '?'. Irrational values are not printed explicitly; they are indicated by a name (capital letters) and used consistently; conjugates and stars indicated by '/ and '*' prefixes. A legend below identifies symbols and may include quadratic representations and Atlas notation when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display (for a character table) — options record and precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Display supports an options record arec to change default style; arec can be passed directly, set as attribute DisplayOptions(tbl), or via global defaults CharacterTableDisplayDefaults.User or .Global (precedence in that order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported arec components: centralizers, characterField, chars, charnames, classes, classnames, indicator, letter, powermap, Display (function called), StringEntry (function for formatting entries), StringEntryData (precomputed data provider), Legend (function to format legend). Each component has specific semantics (e.g., centralizers=false suppresses centralizer printing; powermap can be integer/list/false/"ATLAS"; chars can select characters or replace 'X' by 'Y', etc.). StringEntry is called for each character value and indicator values; StringEntryData called once before display. Legend formats symbol descriptions printed below the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: DisplayOptions attribute
rubrics_metrics.description: DisplayOptions(tbl) is an attribute that can store a record of display options for a character table; there is no default computation method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SetDisplayOptions to set this value; Display will use this attribute value (with the precedence rules) when printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrintCharacterTable
rubrics_metrics.description: PrintCharacterTable(tbl, varname) prints known supported character table attributes in GAP-readable form, binding varname to a character table equivalent to tbl for printed components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used mainly to save character tables to files. The printed output can be read back into GAP to reconstruct the table. For human readable form use Display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default algorithms for computing irreducible characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Several algorithms exist: Dixon‑Schneider is default for arbitrary finite groups; Conlon’s algorithm for supersolvable groups; Baum‑Clausen for abelian‑by‑supersolvable (via IrreducibleRepresentations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions are available as methods for Irr, but explicitly calling one will not set the Irr value of the group automatically. Each algorithm has domain constraints (e.g., Conlon errors if group not solvable; Baum‑Clausen errors if not solvable).

rubrics_metrics.name: IrrDixonSchneider
rubrics_metrics.description: IrrDixonSchneider(G) computes irreducible characters of finite group G using the Dixon‑Schneider method, calling DixonInit and DixonSplit, and returning the list produced by DixontinI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See related sections 71.16–71.19 for details; computation may be expensive for large groups and interacts with Dixon record structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: IrrConlon and IrrBaumClausen
rubrics_metrics.description: IrrConlon(G) returns monomial irreducible characters for solvable G (errors if not solvable); IrrBaumClausen(G) returns absolutely irreducible ordinary characters of G/derived(supersolvable residuum) using Baum‑Clausen algorithm (errors if not solvable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IrrConlon stores monomiality info for each returned irreducible. Both are specialized algorithms for groups with structural constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: IrreducibleRepresentations
rubrics_metrics.description: IrreducibleRepresentations(G[, F]) returns representatives of irreducible matrix representations of G over field F (or complex/cyclotomic numbers if F omitted), up to equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods exist for abelian-by-supersolvable (Baum‑Clausen), for finite F and G using MeatAxe on regular module (may be expensive), and for finite G and F omitted using Dixon method. Representations returned are not guaranteed to preserve unitary forms. IrreducibleModules/IrreducibleRepresentationsDixon may be used for other cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: IrreducibleRepresentationsDixon behaviours and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: IrreducibleRepresentationsDixon(G[, chi]) computes complex irreducible representations via Dixon's method, possibly expensive (may compute subgroup lattice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second argument chi (or list of characters) restricts computation to representations affording those characters. Method may fail if no subgroup exists where a reduction has a linear constituent with multiplicity one. Option unitary requests a unitary representation and errors if one cannot be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: IrreducibleModules / AbsolutelyIrreducibleModules / RegularModule
rubrics_metrics.description: IrreducibleModules(G,F,dim) returns [generators, list of all irreducible modules of dimension dim as MeatAxe modules]. AbsolutelyIrreducibleModules returns absolutely irreducible modules realizable over F up to dimension; RegularModule returns the regular module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synonyms exist for Absolute/Absolutre variants. Outputs are given as MeatAxe modules and useful for module-level computations and for constructing representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dixon record and initialization
rubrics_metrics.description: DixonRecord(G) stores information used by Dixon‑Schneider routines (class arrangement, partial irreducibles, character spaces); DixonInit(G) performs initializations (conjugacy classes, power maps, linear characters, character morphisms) and returns a Dixon record D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dixon record contains components group, conjugacyClasses, irreducibles, characterTable, and function ClassElement(D,el) to identify class numbers. DixonInit may select a prime field and prepare data; the Dixon record accelerates later computations. Interrupting Dixon computations may leave large records; DixontinI cleans unnecessary components.

rubrics_metrics.name: DixonSplit / DixontinI / BestSplittingMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: DixonSplit(D) performs one splitting step selecting a class via BestSplittingMatrix(D), computes the class sum matrix to split character spaces and stores obtained irreducibles; returns class number used or fail. DixontinI(D) finishes the calculation, sorts characters by degree, unbinds unused components and returns list of irreducibles. BestSplittingMatrix(D) chooses class giving best cost/earning split subject to maxclasslen option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global option maxclasslen (default infinity) filters classes considered by BestSplittingMatrix; if no usable class remains BestSplittingMatrix returns fail. Use these functions for interactive / stepwise Dixon calculations; routines assume correctness of provided data and perform little error checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: DxIncludeIrreducibles and SplitCharacters
rubrics_metrics.description: DxIncludeIrreducibles(D, new[, newmod]) adds externally obtained irreducible characters (lists of values relative to D's class arrangement) to the Dixon record and closes them under Galois action and tensoring with linear characters. SplitCharacters(D,list) decomposes given characters according to current character spaces to possibly obtain smaller or irreducible constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: newmod, if given, should be reduced characters corresponding to new; otherwise characters are reduced internally. Splitting is applied only to characters of sufficiently small degree because recalculation is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsDxLargeGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: IsDxLargeGroup(G) returns true if order of group G is smaller than global DXLARGEGROUPORDER; used to decide whether to store a class map in Dixon computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For small groups (true) a class map is stored; for large groups (false) each occurring element is identified individually. This affects memory/time tradeoffs in Dixon computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing character tables from others (direct product)
rubrics_metrics.description: CharacterTableDirectProduct(tbl1, tbl2) constructs the character table of the direct product of tables tbl1 and tbl2; the matrix of irreducibles is the Kronecker product of the irreducibles of the factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Products of ordinary and Brauer tables are supported. Result may not know an underlying group; missing power maps and missing irreducibles of inputs may be computed to construct the product. Embeddings of input tables into the product are stored and can be retrieved with GetFusionMap; if tbl1==tbl2 embeddings distinguished by specification components "1" and "2".
